statement.p: Find the maximum area of a rectangle which is inscribed in {2x^{2}+9y^{2}}=5\text{.}

solution.p: The area of the rectangle is f(x,y)=4xy and the constraint is g(x,y)={2x^{2}+9y^{2}}-5=0\text{.} Due to the Lagrange Multiplier method, we have \vec{\nabla f}=\lambda \vec{\nabla g}\text{,} which gives the following vector equation:
This vector equation is equivalent to these two scalar equations:

p.me: \frac{4y}{4x}=\frac{{4} \lambda x}{{18} \lambda y} \Rightarrow \frac{y}{x}=\frac{{4} x}{{18} y} \Rightarrow y^2=\frac{2}{9} x^2\text{.}

solution.p: Then, we replace this equation into g(x,y)={2x^{2}+9y^{2}}-5=0 to get 2x^2+2x^2=5\text{.} Hence, x=\sqrt{\frac{5}{{4}}} and y=\sqrt{\frac{5}{{18}}} and the maximum area is 4\left(\sqrt{\frac{5}{{4}}}\right)\left(\sqrt{\frac{5}{{18}}}\right)={2.35702}\text{.}

############################################################ # PG Setup Code ############################################################ Context("Numeric"); $a = random(1,4); $b = random(5,10); $c = random(1,10); Context()->variables->are(x=>"Real",y=>"Real"); $constraint = Formula("$a*x^2+$b*y^2")->reduce(); $LM1 = Compute(2*$a); $LM2 = Compute(2*$b); $ans = Compute("(2*$c)/(($a*$b)^(1/2))")->reduce();

BEGIN_PGML Find the maximum area of a rectangle which is inscribed in [`[$constraint]=[$c]\text{.}`]
END_PGML
############################################################ # Solution ############################################################
BEGIN_PGML_SOLUTION The area of the rectangle is [`f(x,y)=4xy`] and the constraint is [`g(x,y)=[$constraint]-[$c]=0\text{.}`] Due to the Lagrange Multiplier method, we have [`\vec{\nabla f}=\lambda \vec{\nabla g}\text{,}`] which gives the following vector equation:
[```\langle 4y, 4x\rangle=\lambda \langle [$LM1] x, [$LM2] y\rangle\text{.}```]
This vector equation is equivalent to these two scalar equations:
[```4y=[$LM1]\lambda x\text{,}```]
[```4x=[$LM2]\lambda y\text{.}```]
We divide the above equations:
[```\newcommand{\R}{\mathbb{R}}\frac{4y}{4x}=\frac{[$LM1] \lambda x}{[$LM2] \lambda y} \Rightarrow \frac{y}{x}=\frac{[$LM1] x}{[$LM2] y} \Rightarrow y^2=\frac{[$a]}{[$b]} x^2\text{.}```]
Then, we replace this equation into [`g(x,y)=[$constraint]-[$c]=0`] to get [`[$a]x^2+[$a]x^2=[$c]\text{.}`] Hence, [`x=\sqrt{\frac{[$c]}{[$LM1]}}`] and [`y=\sqrt{\frac{[$c]}{[$LM2]}}`] and the maximum area is [`4\left(\sqrt{\frac{[$c]}{[$LM1]}}\right)\left(\sqrt{\frac{[$c]}{[$LM2]}}\right)=[$ans]\text{.}`]
END_PGML_SOLUTION
